title: Are SAE Features Stable Under Repeated Training? Characterizing Non-Deterministic Feature Emergence

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if SAE feature discovery is non-deterministic, individual SAE analyses are not reliable descriptions of the model, undermining all SAE-based safety claims.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training 3 separate SAEs from scratch with different seeds, which is compute-intensive and time-consuming. Advanced for beginners within 30 hours.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined comparison (pairwise cosine similarity of decoder vectors across seeds) but training 3 SAEs is the bottleneck. Sustained effort.

novelty.reasoning: This exact question has been comprehensively answered. Paulo and Belrose (2025) 'Sparse Autoencoders Trained on the Same Data Learn Different Features' directly characterizes non-deterministic feature emergence across seeds, measures shared feature fractions, proposes consistency metrics (PW-MCC), and tests across multiple model sizes. The Archetypal SAE paper proposes a solution. The proposed study would fully replicate existing work.

evidence.source: Sparse Autoencoders Trained on the Same Data Learn Different Features (arXiv 2501.16615, 2025)
evidence.finding: Directly studies this question: only 30% of features are shared across different seeds for the largest model tested (Llama 3 8B). Smaller models and smaller SAEs have higher fractions of shared features. Proposes PW-MCC as a metric for consistency.

evidence.source: Archetypal SAE for stable dictionary learning (ICML 2025)
evidence.finding: Identifies SAE instability as a critical limitation and proposes A-SAE to constrain dictionary atoms to the convex hull of training data for stability.
